gen-fs-quilon-gf-yaldevi: A gentle ebb and flow in stroke thickness gives Quilon its editorial authority, with large open counters in the tall letters. Yaldevi stays crisp and oversized in the lowercase, its e opening clearly to the right.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-ol-c: Contemporary and bold, Red Hat Display draws every line like a marker. Daylight fills its curves, while Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails back and makes words read as solid blocks.
gen-fs-rx-100-gf-cascadia-code: Tight, tall, and razor-flat: RX100 looks built in a lab. Cascadia Code draws wire-thin lines and lets each letter sit apart, so paragraphs feel spaced out and easy to scan.
gen-fs-rx-100-gf-julius-sans-one: Compact and crowded, RX100 hits like a punch to the chest. Julius Sans One counters with wide gaps between letters and nearly level capitals and lowercase, so the dense heading gets room to breathe.
gen-fs-rx-100-gf-lexend-peta: Dense and tall with zero stroke variation, RX100 looks stamped. Lexend Peta has wide-mouthed curves that never thin and a generous x-height, loosening things up beside that tight, compact heading.
gen-fs-segment-gf-cascadia-code: Commanding and systematic, Segment leaves wide gaps between letters beneath a middle band so tall that each line looks stocky. Cascadia Code draws glowing neon-tube lines, so reading glides along unhurried.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-supreme: Sharpie leaves only a hairline crack between letters, as if the text were pressed behind a narrow slot. Supreme, with its open, crisp letters, takes well to a little extra size.
gen-fs-sharpie-gf-science-gothic: Squeezed and loud, Sharpie looks pressed behind a narrow slot. Science Gothic has uniform strokes and stroke ends set far apart, for a letter-by-letter feel that loosens up the tight heading.
gen-fs-sharpie-work-sans: Pressed tight and loud, Sharpie leaves barely a hairline between letters. Work Sans bends like a paperclip with no swelling and keeps its c tips well apart, so reading moves along smoothly.
gen-fs-stardom-gf-lexend-mega: Loud and dramatic, Stardom pairs heavy diagonals with hairline strokes. Lexend Mega draws with a single nib and no hairlines, so it looks best given generous size and room beside it.
